headline: Dry sunshine holds through Saturday; Kentucky fog and frost stay localized while a cool northeast-flow wedge strengthens in the Upstate
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: Morning clouds and any river-valley fog are dissipating around Danville and the Bluegrass. High pressure keeps the entire 72-hour period dry, with afternoon temperatures near 70. Chilly clear nights support renewed valley fog and patchy rural frost Friday and Saturday mornings.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 8:55 AM EDT, KDVK was mostly cloudy at 45°F with a 41°F dew point, calm wind and 10-mile visibility. At 9:00 AM, KLEX was mostly cloudy at 46°F with a 43°F dew point, a light northeast wind and 10-mile visibility. Neither official terminal observation showed fog at issuance.

days.label: Thursday
days.hazard: NO OFFICIAL NWS ALERT is active for the Danville point. Earlier river-valley fog is no longer evident at KDVK or KLEX, both reporting 10-mile visibility; no meaningful daytime hazard is expected.
days.forecast: Morning clouds finish clearing, followed by abundant sunshine and light north to northeast wind. Danville's most likely high is 69°F. Tonight turns clear and chilly, with a most likely Danville low near 38°F and colder sheltered valleys supporting patchy frost.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: NO OFFICIAL NWS ALERT is active. Independent analysis highlights patchy river-valley fog and rural frost from approximately 5–9 AM; widespread terminal fog or a hard freeze is not expected.
days.forecast: Patchy valley fog and frost may develop before sunrise, then dissipate by midmorning. The remainder of Friday is sunny and dry with a most likely Danville high near 68°F and a light east to northeast breeze. Friday night is clear and chilly, with a most likely Danville low near 38°F.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: NO OFFICIAL NWS ALERT is active. Patchy frost is possible in the coldest rural valleys early Saturday, but a widespread freeze is not forecast and no daytime hazard is expected.
days.forecast: Any isolated rural frost quickly gives way to full sunshine. Danville's most likely high is near 71°F with very light wind. Saturday night stays mostly clear and seasonably cool, with a most likely low near 41°F.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky remains dry through Saturday. The only meaningful concerns are localized valley fog and patchy rural frost during the early mornings; afternoons are sunny with highs near 70.
kentucky.confidence: High (92%) on dry weather and afternoon clearing; medium-high (80%) on exact overnight lows and the localized coverage of fog and frost.

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: Earlier localized fog near Clemson has cleared, leaving a sunny and mild Thursday. A dry northeast-flow wedge strengthens Friday and Saturday, lowering afternoon temperatures and increasing the breeze while keeping rain out of the forecast.
upstate.currentConditions: At 8:54 AM EDT, KCEU was clear and calm with 10-mile visibility; its latest official report omitted temperature and dew point. At 8:55 AM, KLQK was clear at 45°F with a 43°F dew point, calm wind and 10-mile visibility. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Thursday
days.hazard: NO OFFICIAL NWS ALERT is active for the Clemson point. Earlier localized fog has cleared. An official Increased Fire Danger statement applies to northeast Georgia—not Clemson or Central; only a low-end independent Upstate fire-spread concern remains because very dry afternoon air is paired with light wind.
days.forecast: Sunny skies dominate with a most likely Clemson high near 75°F. Wind remains light from the north to northeast. Clear skies tonight support a most likely Clemson low near 45°F, with sheltered Pickens County locations a few degrees colder.

days.label: Friday
days.hazard: NO OFFICIAL NWS ALERT is active. Independent concern is a modest increase in northeast wind, with afternoon and evening gusts generally 12–22 mph—noticeable but below advisory criteria.
days.forecast: Sunny and cooler as dry cold-air damming becomes established east of the Appalachians. Clemson's most likely high is near 69°F. Northeast wind increases to around 3–9 mph, with occasional gusts of 12–22 mph. Friday night remains clear with a most likely low near 44°F.

days.label: Saturday
days.hazard: NO OFFICIAL NWS ALERT is active. Independent analysis expects a persistent northeast breeze with gusts around 16–26 mph, remaining below wind-advisory criteria.
days.forecast: Sunny but noticeably cooler beneath the dry wedge, with a most likely Clemson high near 66°F. Northeast wind runs 7–13 mph with occasional gusts of 16–26 mph. Saturday night remains clear and cool, with a most likely low near 42°F.

upstate.bottomLine: The Upstate stays dry and sunny. Thursday is the warmest day; a strengthening dry wedge then brings cooler temperatures and a persistent northeast breeze Friday and Saturday without hazardous wind or rain.
upstate.confidence: High (93%) on dry weather and sunshine; medium-high (80%) on Saturday temperatures and peak northeast gusts.

sourceNotes: No official NWS alert is active for either configured point at issuance. NWS Greenville-Spartanburg discusses an official Increased Fire Danger statement for northeast Georgia only; it is not presented as active for Clemson or Central, South Carolina.

College of DuPage radar imagery at 13:25Z showed no organized precipitation over Central Kentucky or Upstate South Carolina. Clean infrared satellite imagery at 13:26Z showed the target regions largely cloud-free after the shallow early fog and low clouds.

The October 22, 2026 Kentucky Weather Center post “Changes Show Up Closer to Halloween” was consulted as independent supplemental analysis. It supports quiet weather through the weekend; its discussion of a more active pattern applies beyond this 72-hour period and is not an official forecast.
KCEU and KLQK supplied timely official Upstate observations. Tempest data was not used for current conditions, calibration or verification.

Official point forecasts, observations, office discussions and all model families agree on a dry 72-hour pattern. All 31 GEFS members were dry on each forecast day. The wider Saturday Upstate temperature spread is represented by the calibrated 63–69°F high range; no unresolved material conflict remains.

HRRR 12Z f18, RAP 11Z f18, NAM 06Z f84, NAM 3-km 06Z f60, GFS 06Z f72, GEFS 06Z f72 and ECMWF IFS 00Z f72 files were verified available from official servers; College of DuPage panels supplied common visual context.
Official NWS alerts and statements are kept separate from independent hazard analysis. Independent fog, frost, fire-spread and wind concerns do not constitute watches, warnings or advisories.
